title: The Group Project Deadline
script: Dian: [thoughtful] Teguh, I need to say this directly: you submitted your section twelve hours before the deadline, and it clearly hadn't been proofread once.
Teguh: I know, and I'm not trying to make excuses, but work genuinely swallowed my entire week.
Dian: [carefully] I understand things come up, but the rest of us restructured our schedules around this deadline, and now the whole group's grade is at risk because of one section.
Teguh: You're right, and I don't have a good counterargument for that, honestly.
Dian: [reflective] I'm not trying to pile on you, I promise, I just don't think it's fair that we all get evaluated as though the work was distributed evenly.
Teguh: Would it help if I rewrote it tonight, properly this time, and you looked it over before we submit the final version?
Dian: [honestly] It would help enormously, actually, provided you're not just telling me what I want to hear right now.
Teguh: I'm not. I genuinely didn't grasp how much the delay would affect everyone else until you laid it out just now.
Dian: [gently] That's part of the problem with group work generally, isn't it? Consequences land on people who had nothing to do with causing them.
Teguh: Fair, though I'd argue the alternative, working entirely alone, would rob us of learning how to actually rely on other people.
Dian: [calmly] That's true, even if right now it feels like a fairly expensive lesson to be learning under deadline pressure.
Teguh: Give me until midnight. I'll send you the revised section, and if it's still not good enough, I'll tell the professor the shortcoming was mine alone, not the group's.
Dian: [encouraging] I appreciate you offering that, though hopefully it won't come to needing it.
Teguh: Hopefully not. And Dian, thank you for saying something instead of just quietly resenting me through the whole presentation.
Dian: [seriously] Believe me, quiet resentment was very much on the table an hour ago.
